name: Cervicoplasty / Cervical contouring
lead: Cervicoplasty is a plastic-surgery term for contouring the neck by working on the skin, fat and sometimes muscle beneath the chin. In aesthetic practice it is part of neck rejuvenation: the goal is a cleaner, more defined line from the chin and jaw into the neck, and it also appears in reconstruction after burn contractures.[1][9][16]

In appearance communities it is grouped among hardmaxxing procedures aimed at a sharper cervicomental angle, the angle between the underside of the chin and the neck that makes a face and jaw read as lean and defined. Surgeons describe the sagging, banded 'turkey gobbler' neck as one of the most common reasons patients see facial plastic surgeons, and direct cervicoplasty, which removes loose neck skin through an incision in the front, is described as an option for a subset of patients who do not want a full facelift.[12][14] A direct neck lift in men has been the subject of dedicated reviews in 2024 and 2026.[13][19]

The published literature consists of surgeon-described techniques, anatomical studies and case series. A 1997 report described a non-excisional anterior approach through a submental incision without removing skin, for patients with good skin contraction, and a ten-year follow-up was later published. Anatomical research has mapped fat compartments of the neck in cadavers.[2][15][3] No randomized trials of aesthetic cervicoplasty were found.

paras: A nonexcisional anterior technique uses a 3 to 4 cm incision behind the submental crease, with a thick subcutaneous flap and endoscope-assisted fat removal, in patients whose skin can redrape [2]. A comprehensive approach to neck rejuvenation emphasises analysis of the lower face and deep structures, and notes bone resorption as a component of aging [4]. A 2021 review addressed optimizing outcomes in neck lift surgery [6]. Other papers examine specific fat compartments, including the subplatysmal supramylohyoid fat [8], and lifting methods such as the MACS-lift [10].

Direct cervicoplasty excises loose anterior neck skin, usually through an incision in or near the submental area, and is described in the literature as an alternative to a full rhytidectomy with periauricular incisions, skin undermining and platysmaplasty for people whose complaint is limited to a sagging anterior neck.[12][14] A 2024 chapter on direct neck lift for men reviews incision options and the scars they leave in the anterior neck, noting that submental fullness varies enough that surgeons benefit from knowing several techniques.[13]

Platysmaplasty, which tightens, repositions or supports the platysma muscle, is usually part of a neck lift. As skin loses elasticity the platysma can separate and show vertical bands, and fullness under the chin may come from tissue beneath the muscle rather than from fat alone, so surgeons plan by identifying which layers contribute. Medial repair brings the central muscle edges together; lateral approaches suspend the muscle to the side; and combined methods address both. One cited comparison found medial repair generally more effective for midline deformity.[16][17]

Cervicoplasty has been combined with thin free flaps, such as anterolateral thigh [1] and thoracodorsal artery perforator flaps [9], to reconstruct postburn neck contractures. These are medical reconstruction series, not cosmetic outcomes.

Risks described for neck lift and platysmaplasty include bleeding or hematoma that may need drainage, infection, numbness from disrupted small sensory nerves, temporary weakness of motor nerves that usually improves, and recurrent platysmal bands or persistent fullness under the chin.[16] Over-resection of fat can leave a contour irregularity sometimes called a 'cobra neck' deformity, and procedures that treat the submandibular glands can produce a fluid collection (sialocele) or lower lip weakness.[16] Direct cervicoplasty leaves a scar on the front of the neck, which is a main consideration discussed for the approach.[13][12]

Neck and submental contour is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as part of overall facial harmony, since a defined neck line makes the jaw and chin appear more prominent. It is treated as a surgical option for people whose neck skin or fat is not addressed by weight loss or non-surgical treatments, and it is often discussed together with chin and jaw implants, liposuction and facelifts.

Studies are small surgical series and anatomical work: seven patients with free anterolateral thigh flap and cervicoplasty [1], a cadaver study of ten heads [3], and technique papers [2][4][10]. One registered trial, NCT05515016, tested a fatty flap from the double chin for chin enhancement in ten participants; the registry lists it as completed [11].

A 10-year follow-up of the non-excisional anterior cervicoplasty was published in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery in 2003, and an anatomical study described the subplatysmal supramylohyoid fat compartment.[15][8]

card.summary: Surgical contouring of neck skin, fat and muscle; documented in surgical series, with little controlled evidence.
card.note: Evidence is surgeon technique papers and small series; the term also covers burn reconstruction.

quick.overview:
Cervicoplasty means reshaping the neck surgically, by managing skin, fat and sometimes muscle. It is used in aesthetic neck lifts and in reconstruction after burns.

The literature is technique descriptions, cadaver work and small series.
quick.mechanism: Surgeons remove or redistribute fat, tighten tissue and may redrape or excise skin, sometimes through a small incision under the chin.
quick.risks: Operative risks apply, and outcomes depend on skin quality as described in technique papers. No randomized trial data were found.

chain: Removes or redistributes submental and neck fat, and tightens platysma and skin
Sharpens the angle between chin and neck
angle.text: Cervicoplasty changes the contour under the chin by removing loose skin or fat and tightening the muscle band. People pursue it to make the jawline and neck look more defined.
